_blockAuthorized: BLOCK-AUTHORIZED: DL-066 keyless hand-solve audit — 31 cases / 162 items, user-authorized read-only audit task (derived independently from exhibits + explanations; no Correct fields consumed)

items.prompt: Enter Motor Division residual income.
items.derivationNotes: RI = Operating Income - (Required Return x Avg Operating Assets) = 420,000 - (0.12 x 2,800,000) = 420,000 - 336,000 = 84,000.

items.prompt: Enter Motor Division ROI percentage as a whole number.
With idle capacity and no opportunity cost, what is the minimum transfer price from the company perspective?
items.derived: 70 variable cost
items.derivationNotes: Minimum transfer price = variable cost + opportunity cost = 70 + 0 (idle capacity) = 70.

items.prompt: Select reasons residual income may improve goal congruence compared with ROI.
items.derivationNotes: Choices 1 (accept projects above required return), 2 (charges for assets employed), and 4 (avoids rejecting value-creating investments) are correct; choice 3 (RI always rises with assets) is false.

items.prompt: Fill in the blank: A transfer price should promote goal _____ so divisional decisions support overall company interests.
items.derived: congruence
items.derivationNotes: A transfer price should promote goal congruence — alignment of divisional incentives with overall company value creation.

items.prompt: Match each measure to the best description.
items.derived: ROI->Operating income divided by assets;Residual income->Income after required asset charge;Minimum transfer price with idle capacity->Variable cost plus opportunity cost;Market price->External benchmark when available
items.derivationNotes: Matched each measure to its defining characteristic per the BSC/transfer-pricing framework.

items.prompt: Enter the unfavorable operating income variance as a positive amount.
items.derivationNotes: Variance = 900,000 target - 840,000 actual = 60,000 unfavorable.

items.prompt: Enter the on-time delivery shortfall in percentage points.
items.derivationNotes: Shortfall = 96% - 91% = 5 percentage points.

items.prompt: Which metric is most clearly a learning and growth measure?
items.derived: Training hours per employee
items.derivationNotes: Training hours per employee is a Learning & Growth measure; operating income is financial, on-time delivery and defect rate are internal process.

items.prompt: Select likely leading indicators of future financial performance.
items.derivationNotes: Defect rate, on-time delivery, and training hours are leading indicators; prior-period operating income is lagging.

items.prompt: Match each scorecard perspective to the best metric.
items.derived: Financial->Operating income;Customer->Customer satisfaction index;Internal process->Defect rate;Learning and growth->Training hours per employee
items.derivationNotes: Financial maps to operating income, customer to customer satisfaction index, internal process to defect rate, learning & growth to training hours.

items.prompt: Which issue should production investigate first?
items.derived: Machine setup errors
items.derivationNotes: Machine setup errors fall within production's span of control per responsibility accounting.

items.prompt: Enter equivalent units for conversion costs using weighted-average.
Enter conversion cost per equivalent unit.
Which operation is the bottleneck?
items.derived: Welding
items.derivationNotes: Welding has the lowest capacity (19,500) — the constraint per TOC.

items.prompt: Select actions consistent with lean thinking.
items.derivationNotes: Reduce waiting (1), investigate rework (3), simplify material movement (4) are lean; increasing batch queues (2) contradicts lean.

items.prompt: Fill in the blank: Equivalent units combine completed units and partially completed work expressed as _____ units.
items.derived: complete
items.derivationNotes: Equivalent units express partial work in terms of complete units.

items.prompt: Match each issue to the best tool.
items.derived: Partially complete WIP->Equivalent units;Lowest capacity resource->Bottleneck analysis;Unnecessary movement->Lean waste review;Continuous homogeneous output->Process costing
items.derivationNotes: Partially complete WIP maps to equivalent units; lowest capacity resource to bottleneck analysis; unnecessary movement to lean waste review; continuous homogeneous output to process costing.

items.prompt: Which control weakness is most directly related to fictitious vendor risk?
items.derived: Same AP clerk can create vendors and enter invoices
items.derivationNotes: The incompatible-duty combination (vendor creation + invoice entry) enables the fictitious vendor scheme end-to-end.

items.prompt: Select controls that would improve the AP process.
items.derivationNotes: Independent vendor-master approval (1), preventive three-way match (2), documented duplicate-report review (4) are correct; post-payment approval (3) is a degradation.

items.prompt: Enter the duplicate/fictitious payment loss as a percentage of pretax income, rounded to one decimal place.
Fill in the blank: Management override and collusion are inherent limitations, so internal control provides reasonable, not _____, assurance.
items.derived: absolute
items.derivationNotes: COSO provides reasonable, not absolute, assurance due to inherent limitations.

items.prompt: Match each control to preventive or detective.
items.derived: Independent vendor approval->Preventive — stops unauthorized vendors from entering the master file before any transaction can be processed;Three-way match before payment->Preventive — blocks improper payment by verifying PO, receiving report, and invoice consistency before cash is disbursed;Duplicate-payment report review->Detective — compares entity cash records to bank records after transactions have cleared, identifying discrepancies that already exist;Bank reconciliation->Detective — compares entity cash records to bank records after transactions have cleared, identifying discrepancies that already exist
items.derivationNotes: Vendor approval and three-way match are preventive; duplicate-payment report review and bank reconciliation are detective (both identify existing discrepancies).

items.prompt: Which evidence issue most weakens operating effectiveness?
items.derived: The report was generated but not reviewed for two months
items.derivationNotes: Documented evidence of non-performance (not reviewed for two months) is the most damaging to operating effectiveness.

items.prompt: Which response best addresses shared administrator IDs?
items.derived: Unique privileged IDs with MFA and periodic access review
items.derivationNotes: Unique IDs + MFA + periodic review establishes individual accountability per COSO Principle 11.

items.prompt: Enter the terminated-user exception rate as a percentage rounded to one decimal place.
Select ITGCs relevant to the exceptions.
items.derivationNotes: Logical access (1), change-management (2), and computer operations/interface monitoring (3) are ITGCs; sales price variance analysis (4) is a business analytics tool.

items.prompt: Fill in the blank: Emergency changes should receive timely post-implementation review and _____.
items.derived: approval
items.derivationNotes: Emergency changes require post-implementation review and approval to complete the control cycle.

items.prompt: Match each exception to the primary risk.
items.derived: Shared administrator IDs->Lack of accountability;Terminated users active->Unauthorized access;Unapproved emergency changes->Unauthorized or erroneous report logic;Failed interface reconciliation->Incomplete or inaccurate data transfer
items.derivationNotes: Shared IDs compromise accountability; terminated users create unauthorized access; unapproved changes risk erroneous report logic; failed reconciliation risks incomplete/inaccurate data transfer.

items.prompt: Why is 14-day log retention a concern?
items.derived: It may prevent investigation of issues discovered after logs are overwritten
items.derivationNotes: 14-day retention means evidence is overwritten before most issues are discovered, preventing investigation.

items.prompt: Based on the scenario, which level of analytics maturity best describes Meridian Retail Group's current state?
items.derived: Descriptive analytics — reporting on historical performance
items.derivationNotes: Meridian uses historical data for monthly variance reports — descriptive analytics (what happened).

items.prompt: The CDO proposes implementing a dashboard that shows real-time sales by region, inventory turnover, and customer foot traffic. What type of analytics does this dashboard primarily enable?
items.derived: Diagnostic analytics — the dashboard allows drill-down to understand performance drivers
items.derivationNotes: Real-time drill-down enables diagnostic analytics (why did it happen).

items.prompt: For the next phase of the analytics roadmap, the CDO wants to use historical sales data and external economic indicators to forecast next quarter's revenue. What type of analytics is being described?
items.derived: Predictive analytics — using historical data and models to forecast future outcomes
items.derivationNotes: Forecasting next quarter's revenue is predictive analytics.

items.prompt: The supply chain team wants a tool that recommends optimal inventory reorder quantities and identifies the most cost-effective shipping routes. The tool should consider demand forecasts, supplier lead times, and freight rates. What type of analytics is required?
items.derived: Prescriptive analytics — recommending optimal actions based on multiple variables and constraints
items.derivationNotes: Recommending optimal actions under constraints is prescriptive analytics.

items.prompt: Before Meridian can advance its analytics maturity, it must address several data challenges. Which of the following is the MOST critical prerequisite for successful analytics implementation?
items.derived: Establishing data governance policies to ensure data quality, consistency, and accessibility across departments
items.derivationNotes: Data governance is the foundational prerequisite; without it, outputs are unreliable regardless of tools or talent.

items.prompt: Calculate the transaction price allocated to the Hardware performance obligation (round to nearest whole dollar).
Calculate the required ending balance in the Allowance for Doubtful Accounts.
Under ASC 606, which criteria indicate a distinct performance obligation?
items.derivationNotes: The two distinctness criteria: customer can benefit on its own (1) and promise separately identifiable (2). Physical delivery (3) and payment (4) are not criteria.

items.prompt: If the unadjusted ADA balance was a $5,000 debit, what is the bad debt expense?
items.derivationNotes: Expense = required credit balance + existing debit = 43,000 + 5,000 = 48,000.

items.prompt: The method of estimating bad debt using an aging schedule is known as the ______ approach.
items.derived: balance sheet
items.derivationNotes: The aging method focuses on the desired ending ADA balance — the balance sheet approach.

items.prompt: Calculate the present value of the lease payments (round to nearest dollar).
items.derivationNotes: 55,000 x 4.212 (PV ordinary annuity, 6%, 5 periods) = 231,660.

items.prompt: Based on ASC 842, how should Meridian classify this lease?
items.derived: Finance lease
items.derivationNotes: PV 231,660 > 90% of fair value (225,000), triggering finance lease classification.

items.prompt: Under ASC 842, the lessee records a lease liability and a ______________ asset on the balance sheet.
items.derived: right-of-use
items.derivationNotes: ASC 842 requires a right-of-use (ROU) asset and lease liability.

items.prompt: What is the lease liability balance at the end of Year 1 after the first payment? (Use the PV calculated previously).
Which of the following are criteria for a finance lease?
items.derivationNotes: Lease term major part of economic life (1), PV >= substantially all FV (2), ownership transfers (3) are criteria; standard asset (4) is not.

items.prompt: Calculate the initial amount of Goodwill recognized on the acquisition date.
Calculate the goodwill impairment loss recognized at the end of Year 2.
items.derivationNotes: Carrying 2,400,000 > FV 2,250,000; impairment = 150,000.

items.prompt: Which of the following would be capitalized as part of the cost of an internally developed patent?
items.derivationNotes: Legal defense costs (1) and registration fees (2) are capitalized; R&D (3) and admin overhead (4) are expensed under ASC 730.

items.prompt: If a reporting unit's fair value is greater than its carrying amount, what is the next step for goodwill impairment testing?
items.derived: No impairment loss is recognized, and no further testing is required
items.derivationNotes: FV > carrying amount means no impairment and no further testing under the one-step test.

items.prompt: Enter total cash collections for January.
Enter total cash disbursements for January.
items.derivationNotes: COGS 390,000 + opex 175,000 + equipment 110,000 = 675,000 (depreciation excluded as non-cash).

items.prompt: Enter the ending cash balance before financing for January. Use a negative sign if the balance is negative.
What amount must Harbor borrow in January to meet the minimum cash balance?
CFO Chen is reviewing the preliminary January forecast. Select the statements that correctly describe how a change would affect the borrowing requirement.
items.derivationNotes: Higher cash-sales % reduces borrowing (1); following-month collection +5% adds 20,000 (3); 5% uncollectible = 20,000 (4). Eliminating borrowing (2) is false — still 15,000 below minimum.

items.prompt: Match each forecast risk to the correct management response.
items.derived: Cash deficit exceeds $100,000 in January->Negotiate extended payment terms with suppliers;December credit collections arrive slower than budgeted->Increase reliance on the line of credit in January;Equipment supplier offers a January discount but payment is due in February->Defer purchase to February, increasing January cash available;Actual January sales exceed budget by 15%->Increase both collections and COGS projections in the forecast
items.derivationNotes: Deficit >100k triggers supplier negotiation; slower collections require more credit; deferring purchase preserves cash; higher sales update both collections and COGS.

items.prompt: Enter the budgeted direct labor cost for July.
Enter the total budgeted manufacturing overhead cost for July (variable + fixed).
Enter the predetermined total overhead rate per direct labor hour using denominator activity.
What effect would adding a second shift in September have on budgeted fixed overhead cost?
items.derived: Total fixed overhead cost remains unchanged; per-unit fixed overhead decreases
items.derivationNotes: Fixed overhead is a capacity cost, constant within the relevant range; per-unit decreases as volume rises.

items.prompt: Select the true statements about manufacturing overhead budgeting.
items.derivationNotes: Fixed OH per unit falls with volume (1); rate set before period (2); applied = rate x actual activity (3). Variable OH not in rate (4) is false.

items.prompt: Match each budget component to its correct calculation formula.
items.derived: Direct labor budget->Units produced x DLH per unit x Wage rate;Variable overhead budget->Actual DLH x Variable OH rate per DLH;Fixed overhead budget->Remains constant within the relevant range;Applied manufacturing overhead->Predetermined OH rate x Actual activity
items.derivationNotes: DL budget = units x DLH/unit x wage rate; VOH = actual DLH x variable rate; FOH constant; applied = predetermined rate x actual activity.

items.prompt: Using the information in Exhibit 1, what is Division A's return on investment for the current year?
What is Division A's residual income for the current year?
If the proposed $500,000 investment is accepted, what will Division A's new ROI be?
If Division A is evaluated using residual income, should the manager accept the proposed $500,000 investment?
items.derived: Yes, because residual income will increase by $20,000

items.prompt: Which division had the best performance based on residual income?
items.derived: Division A
items.derivationNotes: RI: A = 120,000, B = 50,000, C = 0; Division A is highest.

items.prompt: The production manager notes that actual revenue exceeded the static budget by $126,000 and believes performance was strong. However, the controller points out that actual sales volume was 12,000 units compared to the budgeted 10,000. Based on Exhibit 1, what is the sales volume variance for operating income?
items.derived: Favorable $50,000 — the flexible budget shows expected operating income at 12,000 units is $80,000, compared to static budget operating income of $30,000, yielding a $50,000 favorable volume variance
items.derivationNotes: Volume variance = (12,000-10,000) x $25 CM = 50,000 F, or flexible OI 80,000 - static OI 30,000 = 50,000 F.

items.prompt: Using Exhibit 1 and Exhibit 2, compute the flexible budget variance for direct materials. Compare actual direct materials cost to the flexible budget amount at 12,000 units.
items.derived: Unfavorable $12,000 — flexible budget DM = 12,000 × $20 = $240,000; actual DM = $252,000; variance = $252,000 − $240,000 = $12,000 unfavorable (actual cost exceeded the flexible budget)
items.derivationNotes: Flexible budget DM = 12,000 x 20 = 240,000; actual 252,000; variance 12,000 U.

items.prompt: The controller identified several variances. Which of the following statements correctly interpret the variance results shown in Exhibit 1? (Select all that apply.)
items.derivationNotes: Volume variance favorable (1); selling price variance 24,000 U (3); FOH variance 5,000 U (4); total variable cost variance 8,000 U (5). DL variance is actually 12,000 F, not U (2 is wrong).

items.prompt: Match each variance description to the correct variance formula for Precision Manufacturing's standard costing system.
items.derived: Difference between actual revenue and flexible budget revenue at 12,000 units->Selling price variance — (Actual Price − Standard Price) × Actual Quantity = ($73 − $75) × 12,000 = $24,000 U;Difference between flexible budget variable cost at 12,000 units and actual variable cost->Flexible budget variable cost variance — Sum of (actual cost − standard cost × actual units) for DM, DL, VOH, VS&A;Difference between static budget operating income and flexible budget operating income->Sales volume variance — (Actual Units − Budgeted Units) × Standard Contribution Margin per Unit = (12,000 − 10,000) × $25 = $50,000 F;Difference between actual fixed overhead and budgeted fixed overhead->Fixed overhead spending variance — Actual FOH − Budgeted FOH = $185,000 − $180,000 = $5,000 U
items.derivationNotes: Actual-vs-flexible revenue = selling price variance; flexible-vs-actual variable cost = flexible budget variance; static-vs-flexible OI = sales volume variance; actual-vs-budgeted FOH = spending variance.

items.prompt: The production manager is evaluated based on the flexible budget variance for manufacturing costs. Which statement BEST explains why the flexible budget is more appropriate than the static budget for evaluating the production manager's cost control?
items.derived: The flexible budget adjusts allowed costs to actual production volume, so the production manager is evaluated only on cost elements within their control (price and efficiency), not on volume changes that are typically outside production management's control
items.derivationNotes: Flexible budget isolates cost control (price/efficiency) from volume, which the production manager cannot control.

items.prompt: Calculate the Variable Overhead Spending Variance (enter unfavorable as positive, favorable as negative, or just absolute value).
items.derivationNotes: Actual VOH 31,000 - standard for actual hours (9,800x3=29,400) = 1,600 U.

items.prompt: Calculate the Variable Overhead Efficiency Variance.
Calculate the Fixed Overhead Production-Volume Variance.
Calculate the Fixed Overhead Spending (Budget) Variance.
items.derivationNotes: Actual 52,000 - budgeted 50,000 = 2,000 U.

items.prompt: Which variance is NEVER considered controllable by the production supervisor?
items.derived: Fixed overhead production-volume variance
items.derivationNotes: The volume variance reflects capacity utilization (a management decision), not shop-floor cost control.

items.prompt: Summit Electronics' internal audit team has identified inconsistent tone at the middle, where plant managers tolerate minor inventory discrepancies. Which COSO component is primarily affected by this deficiency?
items.derived: Control Environment — management's philosophy and operating style set the tone for control consciousness
items.derivationNotes: Tone at the middle (management attitude/operating style) is a Control Environment issue.

items.prompt: The internal audit team noted that Summit Electronics' risk assessment does not specifically address financial reporting risks for new contracts. Which COSO principle is most directly violated by this gap?
items.derived: The organization identifies and assesses changes that could significantly impact the system of internal control
items.derivationNotes: Failure to assess risks from new contracts violates COSO Principle 9.

items.prompt: Summit Electronics has strong automated controls over accounts payable (three-way match) but no controls over manual journal entries. According to the COSO framework, which statement BEST describes the implication of this gap?
items.derived: Control activities should be designed at various levels, including both automated and manual controls, to address all relevant risks
items.derivationNotes: Strong controls in one area do not compensate for missing controls in another; manual journal entries need specific controls.

items.prompt: Summit Electronics lacks a formal whistleblower hotline and communicates policies only on an ad hoc basis. Which COSO principle is MOST directly affected by these gaps?
items.derived: The organization communicates internal control information to personnel, including their roles and responsibilities in the internal control system
items.derivationNotes: Ad hoc communication and no hotline violate the Information and Communication requirements.

items.prompt: Summit Electronics relies on quarterly internal audit reviews and annual external audits for monitoring, with no ongoing monitoring of controls. According to the COSO framework, which statement is MOST accurate?
items.derived: Monitoring activities should include both ongoing evaluations (built into operations) and separate evaluations (periodic audits) to provide timely feedback on control effectiveness
items.derivationNotes: Monitoring should include both ongoing and separate evaluations; relying solely on periodic audits lets deficiencies go undetected.

items.prompt: The IT steering committee is evaluating different cloud service models for MedTech's applications. Using Exhibit 1, match each application requirement to the most appropriate cloud service model.
items.derived: The HR department needs a payroll and benefits administration system; they want to avoid any hardware or software management and access it through a web browser->SaaS — software is fully managed by the vendor and accessed via browser; the customer manages only data and user access;The IT team wants to build a custom inventory management application; they need a platform with development tools, database, and middleware but want to avoid managing underlying infrastructure->PaaS — provides development platform and runtime environment; vendor manages infrastructure, OS, and middleware; customer manages applications and data;The data science team needs raw virtual servers, storage, and networking to run analytics workloads; they will manage the OS and applications themselves->IaaS — provides virtualized computing resources; customer manages OS, middleware, runtime, applications, and data; vendor manages physical infrastructure;The ERP system contains sensitive financial and patient data; MedTech needs maximum control and is considering keeping it on-premise->On-premise — maximum control over all layers; customer manages everything including physical security; appropriate for highly regulated data
items.derivationNotes: HR (browser, no management) -> SaaS; IT (dev platform, no infrastructure) -> PaaS; data science (raw servers) -> IaaS; ERP (sensitive, max control) -> On-premise.

items.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, the CFO asks whether cloud migration makes financial sense. Which statement BEST analyzes the financial impact of migrating from on-premise to IaaS?
items.derived: IaaS offers significant long-term savings ($460,000/year in steady state) but requires $190,000 in one-time migration costs; the 5-month payback period is attractive, and the ongoing operational savings (reduced IT staff, no facility costs, lower downtime) support the business case
items.derivationNotes: IaaS steady-state saves 460,000/yr with ~5-month payback on 190,000 migration cost.

items.prompt: The compliance officer raises concerns about data security and regulatory compliance in the cloud. Based on Exhibit 1 and general cloud computing knowledge, which of the following are VALID concerns that MedTech should address in its cloud migration plan? (Select all that apply.)
items.derivationNotes: Data responsibility (1), data residency (2), SOC 2 reports (3), and vendor lock-in (4) are valid; 'cloud eliminates internal controls' is the distractor.

items.prompt: MedTech's controller is concerned about capitalizing cloud implementation costs versus expensing them. Under current accounting guidance (ASC 350-40), which statement BEST describes how MedTech should account for the cloud migration costs shown in Exhibit 2?
items.derived: Cloud implementation costs should be accounted for based on the nature of the cost — subscription fees are expensed as incurred; one-time migration costs (data migration, training) should be evaluated under the hosting arrangement guidance, with certain implementation costs capitalized if the arrangement is a service contract
items.derivationNotes: ASC 350-40: subscription fees expensed; certain implementation costs of a service contract may be capitalized.

items.prompt: The IT steering committee is considering different cloud deployment models. Match each deployment model to the scenario that BEST fits its characteristics.
items.derived: MedTech's ERP system must comply with strict FDA and HIPAA requirements; the company wants dedicated infrastructure but has no need for a massive capital investment in a new data center->Private cloud — dedicated infrastructure for a single organization; provides the highest security and compliance control while avoiding data center capital costs;MedTech's R&D team needs a sandbox environment to test new analytics tools; they want low cost and do not need dedicated infrastructure->Public cloud — resources shared across multiple organizations; lowest cost but least control; appropriate for development, testing, and non-sensitive workloads;MedTech and two other medical device companies want to share a cloud environment that meets their common regulatory requirements while keeping costs lower than a fully private cloud->Community cloud — shared infrastructure among several organizations with common compliance concerns (e.g., HIPAA, FDA); balances cost and compliance;MedTech acquired a small distributor and needs to quickly integrate their IT systems without a long capital approval process->Public cloud (rapid deployment) — quick provisioning, pay-as-you-go pricing; ideal for acquisitions, temporary workloads, or rapid scaling without capital investment
items.derivationNotes: ERP (dedicated, compliance) -> Private cloud; R&D sandbox (low cost) -> Public cloud; shared regulated environment -> Community cloud; acquisition (rapid deployment) -> Public cloud rapid deployment.

items.prompt: Calculate the total Comprehensive Income for the year.
items.derivationNotes: NI 500,000 + OCI (AFS 40,000 - translation 30,000 = 10,000) = 510,000. Trading gains already in NI.

items.prompt: Which of the following items bypass the income statement and go directly to Other Comprehensive Income (OCI)?
items.derivationNotes: AFS gains/losses (1), foreign currency translation (2), and pension prior service costs (3) are OCI; trading securities (4) go to NI and dividends (5) to retained earnings.

items.prompt: What is the total reduction to Stockholders' Equity resulting from the treasury stock purchase?
items.derivationNotes: 10,000 shares x $15 = 150,000 (cost method, contra-equity for full cost).

items.prompt: If Silverline used the par value method instead of the cost method for treasury stock, how would the initial purchase affect total stockholders' equity?
items.derived: The total reduction to equity would be exactly the same
items.derivationNotes: Total dollars removed (cash paid 150,000) is the same under both methods; only account distribution differs.

items.prompt: Comprehensive income includes all changes in equity during a period except those resulting from investments by and distributions to _________.
items.derived: owners
items.derivationNotes: Comprehensive income excludes investments by and distributions to owners.

items.prompt: Calculate the cash interest payment made every six months.
Calculate the issue price of the bonds (round to nearest whole dollar).
Calculate the interest expense to be recorded for the first six months (ending June 30, Year 1).
Calculate the carrying value of the bond immediately after the first interest payment on June 30.
How are bond issue costs treated under current US GAAP?
items.derived: Deducted from the carrying value of the bond liability
items.derivationNotes: Under ASU 2015-03, bond issue costs are a direct deduction from the bond liability's carrying value.

items.prompt: Calculate the variable cost per machine hour using the High-Low method.
Calculate the total fixed cost using the High-Low method.
What is the estimated total cost for 7,000 hours using the Regression model?
What does the R-squared value of 0.85 indicate?
items.derived: 85% of the variation in total cost is explained by machine hours
items.derivationNotes: R-squared is the proportion of variance in the dependent variable explained by the independent variable.

items.prompt: What are the primary disadvantages of the High-Low method compared to regression?
items.derivationNotes: Uses only two data points (1) and is influenced by outliers (2); it is simple (3 false) and does separate costs (4 false).

items.prompt: Enter the ending inventory balance at March 31.
Enter the ending accounts receivable balance at March 31 (gross, before allowance for doubtful accounts).
Enter the ending accounts payable balance at March 31.
Enter the ending cash balance at March 31.
Which budgeted financial statement item is NOT directly affected by the sales collection assumption?
items.derived: Ending inventory balance
items.derivationNotes: Inventory is determined by purchases and COGS, not by collection patterns.

items.prompt: Match each budgeted balance sheet line item to the primary budget or policy that determines it.
items.derived: Cash->Cash budget and collection/disbursement timing;Accounts receivable->Sales budget and credit collection policy;Inventory->Cost of goods sold budget and purchases budget;Accounts payable->Purchases budget and supplier payment terms
items.derivationNotes: Cash -> cash budget; A/R -> sales/collection policy; inventory -> COGS + purchases; A/P -> purchases + payment terms.

items.prompt: Summit Furniture's Cutting Department can theoretically produce 50,000 units per year. After accounting for scheduled maintenance (2,000 hours), employee breaks and shift changes (1,500 hours), and machine setup time (3,500 hours), the practical capacity is 38,000 units. Which capacity measure should Summit use for fixed overhead allocation to BEST approximate the cost of unused capacity?
items.derived: Practical capacity — it represents the maximum sustainable production under realistic operating conditions; using practical capacity highlights the cost of unused capacity (the difference between practical and actual) and avoids distorting product costs with the cost of idle facilities
items.derivationNotes: Practical capacity best approximates the cost of unused capacity (the conceptually best denominator level).

items.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, what would be the difference in the fixed overhead volume variance if Summit Furniture changed its denominator level from practical capacity (38,000 units) to master-budget capacity (30,000 units)?
items.derived: The volume variance would decrease from $500,000 unfavorable to $126,667 unfavorable — a $373,333 reduction — because a lower denominator level reduces the fixed overhead rate per unit and decreases the unfavorable volume variance
items.derivationNotes: Practical (38,000-28,000)x50 = 500,000 U; master-budget (30,000-28,000)x63.33 = 126,667 U; variance decreases by 373,333.

items.prompt: The CFO is evaluating the implications of the capacity denominator level choice. Which of the following statements correctly describe the impact of different capacity measures? (Select all that apply.)
items.derivationNotes: DL-047-suspect. Correct accounting: theoretical capacity (50,000) gives the LOWEST rate ($38) and largest variance, so statement 1 (theoretical = highest rate) is FALSE. Only statement 3 (volume variance zero when denominator = actual) is correct. Statements 2, 4, 5 are wrong per the explanation.

items.prompt: The CFO must recommend a capacity management strategy for each department. Match each department's situation to the most appropriate capacity strategy using Exhibit 1.
items.derived: Cutting Department — practical capacity is 38,000 but actual is only 28,000; 10,000 units of capacity are idle->Reduce unused capacity — investigate why 26% of practical capacity is idle; consider using excess capacity for new products or outsourcing selected operations to fill the gap;Assembly Department — practical capacity is 42,000; this is the highest capacity in the plant; other departments limit total output to 28,000->Identify as the bottleneck — this department currently does not limit output, but management should monitor it to ensure Assembly remains the constraint;Finishing Department — practical capacity is 40,000; new equipment would increase capacity to 55,000 but cost $2.5M->Defer capital investment — current capacity exceeds demand; investing in additional capacity would increase fixed costs without increasing throughput;All departments — Summit's management wants to understand the true cost of carrying unused capacity over the business cycle->Use normal capacity for strategic planning — 32,000 units reflects average long-term demand; compare actual to normal to assess capacity utilization over the business cycle
items.derivationNotes: Cutting (idle) -> reduce unused capacity; Assembly (highest, not constraint) -> monitor; Finishing (excess) -> defer capital; All (true cost of unused capacity) -> normal capacity for planning.

items.prompt: Summit's CFO must recommend a denominator level to the board. The board is concerned about minimizing unfavorable volume variances to avoid explaining large write-offs to investors. Which recommendation BEST balances board concerns with sound accounting practice?
items.derived: Use practical capacity and clearly disclose the cost of unused capacity as a separate line item in the management discussion — this provides transparency about capacity utilization and avoids distorting product costs while still informing investors about operational efficiency
items.derivationNotes: Practical capacity is conceptually sound; transparently disclose unused-capacity cost rather than hiding it via a lower denominator.

items.prompt: The internal audit team identified several scenarios where application controls should prevent or detect errors. Match each scenario to the appropriate application control from Exhibit 1.
items.derived: An accounts payable clerk accidentally enters $25,000 instead of $2,500 for the unit price of a surgical instrument on a purchase order->Purchase order limit check — the entered unit price ($25,000) exceeds the 20% threshold above the expected price, triggering a rejection;A data entry operator creates an invoice referencing a vendor ID that does not exist in the approved vendor master table->Vendor master validity check — the system verifies the vendor ID against the approved master table and rejects the invoice when no match is found;An order entry clerk enters a customer account number as 48219 instead of 48129 — a transposition of two digits->Check digit validation — the modulus-10 algorithm detects the transposition error and rejects the account number as invalid;An order processor attempts to enter a sales order for a customer whose outstanding balance already exceeds the approved credit limit->Customer credit limit check — the system blocks the order and notifies the order processor that the credit limit would be exceeded
items.derivationNotes: Wrong price -> PO limit check; invalid vendor ID -> vendor master validity; transposition -> check digit; over credit limit -> credit limit check.

items.prompt: The internal audit team discovers that the three-way match control (matching PO, receiving report, and invoice) can be overridden by senior procurement managers. In the past 6 months, the override has been used 47 times for one particular vendor. Which control risk does this situation represent?
items.derived: Control override by management — the three-way match is a key detective/preventive control; frequent overrides indicate that the control is not operating effectively and may allow erroneous or fraudulent payments to bypass control
items.derivationNotes: Frequent management overrides (47 times, one vendor) indicate a control override risk.

items.prompt: The ERP system includes processing controls in addition to input controls. According to Exhibit 2, which of the following are examples of processing controls that MedTech should have in place? (Select all that apply.)
items.derivationNotes: Run-to-run totals (1), sequence checks (2), reasonableness checks (4) are processing controls; weekly payment report review (3) is output and login screen (5) is access.

items.prompt: MedTech's internal audit team is classifying application controls by type. Match each control description to the correct control category using Exhibit 2.
items.derived: When a receiving clerk enters the quantity received, the ERP system verifies that it does not exceed the quantity ordered by more than 10%->Input control — quantity reasonableness check prevents receiving errors from entering the system;The ERP system assigns sequential batch numbers to all invoice batches; the accounting supervisor reviews a daily gap report for missing batches->Processing control — batch sequence verification ensures no invoice batches are lost or deleted during processing;The accounts payable manager reviews a weekly aged payables report and investigates any invoices older than 45 days->Output control — periodic review of processed output ensures accuracy and triggers follow-up on anomalies;The ERP system restricts invoice entry to users in the AP Clerk role; procurement managers cannot enter invoices->Access control — role-based security prevents users from performing incompatible functions
items.derivationNotes: Receiving quantity check -> input; batch sequence -> processing; aged payables review -> output; role restriction -> access.

items.prompt: The same employee in MedTech's AP department can create new vendor records, enter invoices, and process payments in the ERP system. Management argues that the system's input controls (vendor validity check, three-way match) compensate for this lack of segregation. Which assessment BEST reflects the internal control risk?
items.derived: Segregation of duties is severely compromised — one employee has end-to-end control over the vendor lifecycle (create, pay, reconcile); application controls reduce but do not eliminate the fraud risk, as the employee could create a fictitious vendor and process payments while manually overriding the three-way match
items.derivationNotes: One employee controlling the entire vendor lifecycle is a severe SOD compromise; application controls reduce but do not eliminate the risk.

items.prompt: Referring to Exhibit 1, the sales manager paid $500 to a customs official to expedite clearance of a shipment of emergency replacement parts. The payment was recorded as "expediting fee" in the books. Under the FCPA, which statement BEST characterizes this payment?
items.derived: This may qualify as a facilitating payment if it was for a routine, non-discretionary government action (processing customs clearance) and was accurately recorded — however, the company should establish clear policies defining when facilitating payments are acceptable and require documentation
items.derivationNotes: Facilitating payments for routine non-discretionary actions are a narrow FCPA exception, but must be recorded and governed by policy.

items.prompt: Apex's internal audit team discovers that the 15% commission paid to Agent X in Country X (Exhibit 1) was routed through a shell company in a third country and there is no written agreement defining the services provided. The agent is a cousin of the country's minister of procurement. What is the MOST significant FCPA risk?
items.derived: This presents a high-risk red flag for indirect bribery — the FCPA prohibits corrupt payments through third parties; the combination of relationship to a government official, opaque payment structure, and lack of written agreement strongly suggests the commission may be a conduit for improper payments
items.derivationNotes: Third-party intermediary with official relationship, shell company, no written agreement = high-risk indirect bribery red flag.

items.prompt: Based on Exhibit 1 and Exhibit 2, which of the following actions should Apex Components take to strengthen its FCPA compliance program? (Select all that apply.)
items.derivationNotes: Due diligence (1), training (2), controlled facilitating payments (4), terminate high-risk JV partner (5) are correct; ignoring the donation (3) is wrong.

items.prompt: The internal audit team classified each risk scenario from Exhibit 1 for further action. Match each scenario to the most appropriate compliance response.
items.derived: Customs expediting fee — $500 paid to customs official; recorded as expense->Permissible if properly approved and documented under company policy — establish clear policy on facilitating payments; continue monitoring;Agent commission — 15% via shell company; agent related to procurement minister->Investigate immediately and consider termination — red flags indicate likely improper payments; may require voluntary disclosure to DOJ;Charitable donation request — $50,000 to minister's personal foundation->Decline and report to compliance committee — donation to personal entity of government official is presumptively improper; offer alternative legitimate charitable options;Luxury client entertainment — $1,200/person including spouses for government clients->Review and strengthen expense policy — entertainment exceeding $500 per person should require pre-approval; spouse attendance is presumptively improper
items.derivationNotes: Customs fee -> facilitating-payment policy; agent commission -> investigate/terminate; donation -> decline/report; entertainment -> strengthen expense policy.

items.prompt: Apex's CFO argues that the company does not need separate FCPA-specific internal controls because the company already has a general internal control system. Referring to Exhibit 2, which response BEST addresses this argument?
items.derived: The FCPA's accounting provisions specifically require issuers to maintain internal accounting controls sufficient to provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements and to maintain accountability for assets — general controls may not be sufficient to detect and prevent improper foreign payments that could be disguised in the books
items.derivationNotes: FCPA accounting provisions require issuers to maintain controls sufficient to ensure proper recording; general controls may not address FCPA-specific risks.

items.prompt: Match each IIA Standard category to the type of guidance it provides.
items.derived: Attribute Standards->Define the characteristics and capabilities required for internal audit activities and individuals;Performance Standards->Describe the nature of internal audit work and quality criteria for measuring performance;Implementation Standards->Apply Attribute and Performance Standards to specific engagement types such as assurance or consulting
items.derivationNotes: Attribute = characteristics/capabilities; Performance = nature of work; Implementation = apply to specific engagement types.

items.prompt: The internal audit department previously performed consulting engagements for the lending department. Based on IIA Standards, which action is MOST critical for preserving objectivity?
items.derived: Prohibit internal auditors from performing assurance engagements in the lending department for a reasonable period after performing consulting work there
items.derivationNotes: A cooling-off period (IIA 1130) is the appropriate safeguard against the familiarity threat.

items.prompt: The CAE has drafted a revised internal audit charter for Audit Committee approval. Based on IIA Standards, which elements MUST be included? (Select all that apply.)
items.derivationNotes: Charter must define purpose/authority/responsibility (1), reporting relationships (2), and scope (3). Annual review (4) and methodology (5) are not mandated.

items.prompt: Under the IIA Standards, which reporting structure best supports internal audit independence at First Continental Bank?
items.derived: CAE reports functionally to the Audit Committee and administratively to the CEO, with direct access to the Audit Committee chair for sensitive matters
items.derivationNotes: IIA 1110 requires functional reporting to the board/audit committee and administrative reporting to the CEO.

items.prompt: The CAE needs to establish a Quality Assurance and Improvement Program (QAIP) under IIA Standards. Which of the following are required QAIP components? (Select all that apply.)
items.derivationNotes: Ongoing internal monitoring (1), external assessments every 5 years (2), internal self-assessments (3) are required; performance metrics (4) and benchmarking (5) are not.

items.prompt: The CISO is preparing an incident report for the board. Match each cybersecurity threat type to its role in the CCHS incident.
items.derived: Phishing email->The initial attack vector — a deceptive email with a malicious attachment bypassed human controls and delivered the trojan to the billing workstation;Remote Access Trojan (RAT)->The persistence mechanism — remained undetected for 48 hours, exfiltrated credentials, and provided remote access for lateral movement;Ransomware->The final payload — encrypted files across the network causing a 22-day operational outage and $18.2 million in estimated losses;DDoS (distraction attack)->A coordinated traffic flood against the patient portal designed to divert IT resources during the ransomware deployment
items.derivationNotes: Phishing = initial vector; RAT = persistence; ransomware = final payload; DDoS = distraction.

items.prompt: Based on the incident timeline, which control failure was the MOST critical enabler of the ransomware attack at CCHS?
items.derived: Lack of mandatory cybersecurity awareness training — the phishing email was the initial attack vector, and without training, the employee had no basis to recognize the social engineering indicators
items.derivationNotes: The attack chain began with phishing that succeeded because no awareness training had been conducted.

items.prompt: Using Exhibit 2 data, the CISO proposes implementing MFA for all internal system access at a cost of $420,000 annually. Based on the incident, the probability of a similar attack in any given year without MFA is estimated at 12%, and with MFA it drops to 3%. Using expected value analysis, calculate the annual net benefit (or cost) of implementing MFA. The $18.2 million total loss is the exposure for a successful attack. Enter your answer as the nearest whole number in dollars. If the net benefit is negative, include the minus sign. Do not use commas or dollar signs.
items.derivationNotes: Expected loss without MFA = 18.2M x 12% = 2,184,000; with MFA = 18.2M x 3% = 546,000; benefit 1,638,000 - cost 420,000 = 1,218,000.

items.prompt: Based on Exhibit 2, which control improvements should CCHS implement to prevent a recurrence? (Select all that apply.)
items.derivationNotes: Awareness training (1), EDR (2), network segmentation (3), 3-2-1 backups (4) address gaps; incident reports (5) and internet restriction (6) do not prevent recurrence.

items.prompt: The board asks whether paying the ransom was the right decision. Based on cybersecurity best practices and internal control principles, which response is MOST appropriate?
items.derived: The decision to pay should be made collaboratively with law enforcement, cybersecurity experts, and legal counsel, considering data backups, decryption feasibility, and regulatory obligations — but prevention through layered controls is always the superior strategy
items.derivationNotes: Best practice is a structured, collaborative decision; prevention via layered controls is always superior.

items.prompt: DataBridge Solutions Inc. has been found by a EU supervisory authority to have intentionally violated EU data subjects' rights under Article 83(5) of the GDPR. Based on the financial data provided in Exhibit 1, what is the maximum potential administrative fine DataBridge faces?
Using the data in Exhibit 1, what is the expected annual net benefit (or cost) of implementing the proposed privacy compliance program? (Expected value of avoided losses minus program cost.)

DataBridge discovers that an employee inadvertently exposed a database containing personal data of 3,200 EU data subjects. Under the GDPR, within how many hours must DataBridge notify the appropriate supervisory authority of this data breach?
items.derived: 72 hours
items.derivationNotes: GDPR Article 33(1) requires notification within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach.

items.prompt: An EU data subject submits a request to DataBridge demanding that the company delete all personal data collected about them and cease processing. Under the GDPR, which data subject right has been invoked?
items.derived: Right to erasure (right to be forgotten)
items.derivationNotes: The right to erasure (right to be forgotten) under GDPR Article 17.

items.prompt: DataBridge needs to transfer personal data of EU customers from its Irish subsidiary to its primary data center in Chicago for centralized analytics processing. Which GDPR-approved transfer mechanism is most appropriate for this recurring data transfer scenario?
items.derived: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs)
items.derivationNotes: SCCs are the standard transfer mechanism for routine B2B transfers to countries without an adequacy decision.

items.prompt: OmniRetail's demand forecasting model requires historical sales data with known actual demand to predict future sales. Which type of machine learning does this approach represent?
items.derived: Supervised learning
items.derivationNotes: Demand forecasting uses labeled historical data with known outcomes — supervised learning.

items.prompt: For each machine learning application at OmniRetail, select whether it uses supervised or unsupervised learning.
items.derived: Demand forecasting->Supervised learning — regression model trained on historical sales data with known outcomes to predict future demand;Fraud detection->Supervised learning — classification model trained on labeled transaction histories identifying which transactions were fraudulent;Customer segmentation->Unsupervised learning — clustering algorithm grouping customers by purchasing behavior without pre-labeled categories;Anomaly detection->Unsupervised learning — outlier detection identifying unusual transaction patterns without prior fraud labels
items.derivationNotes: Demand forecasting and fraud detection are supervised (labeled data); segmentation and anomaly detection are unsupervised (unlabeled).

items.prompt: The data science team observes that the demand forecasting model performs poorly on stores with limited historical data. Which of the following factors are likely contributing to overfitting in the model? (Select all that apply.)
items.derivationNotes: Insufficient data (1), excessive complexity (2), learning noise (3) contribute to overfitting; a simpler model (4) reduces it.

items.prompt: OmniRetail's fraud detection model uses machine learning rather than a traditional rule-based system with fixed thresholds. What is the primary advantage of the ML approach for this application?
items.derived: ML models can adapt to evolving fraud patterns by learning from new transaction data without manual rule updates
items.derivationNotes: ML continuously learns from new data and detects novel patterns that rule-based systems would miss.

items.prompt: OmniRetail's customer segmentation model identified 12 distinct customer clusters using unsupervised learning. Which of the following are valid retail business applications of these segmentation results? (Select all that apply.)
items.derivationNotes: Targeted marketing (1), merchandising (2), and customer acquisition (3) are valid; setting inventory reorder quantities (4) requires demand forecasting.

items.prompt: The CFO's team is preparing a training deck on RPA for the audit committee. Match each RPA characteristic to its correct description.
items.derived: Rule-based processing->RPA bots execute predefined, structured steps following explicit business rules without deviation or judgment;User interface interaction->RPA bots interact with applications through the same user interface as human users, requiring no system integration changes;Exception handling->Bots flag transactions that fall outside predefined parameters for human review, with automated routing to the appropriate team member;Attended vs unattended mode->Attended bots run on user desktops with human triggers; unattended bots run on servers on scheduled intervals without human intervention
items.derivationNotes: Rule-based -> predefined steps; UI interaction -> same UI as humans; exception handling -> flag for review; attended/unattended -> desktop vs server.

items.prompt: Based on the data in Exhibit 1, which finance process is the STRONGEST candidate for RPA implementation at Meridian?
items.derived: Invoice data entry to ERP — it is high-volume (3,750 per month), entirely rule-based with structured data, and has the second-lowest exception rate at 4%
items.derivationNotes: Invoice data entry meets all RPA suitability criteria (high volume, rule-based, structured, low exceptions).

items.prompt: Using the scenario data, calculate the annual net benefit (annual benefits minus annual ongoing costs) for the RPA initiative in Year 2, after implementation costs have been incurred. Enter your answer as a whole number in dollars. Do not use commas or dollar signs.
Which of the following processes from Exhibit 1 are appropriate candidates for RPA? (Select all that apply.)
items.derivationNotes: Invoice entry (1), bank rec (2), intercompany matching (3), journal entry (4) are suitable; loss reserve estimation (5) requires judgment and has 35% exceptions.

items.prompt: Based on Exhibit 2, which internal control enhancement is MOST critical to address the segregation of duties (SOD) risk created by the RPA implementation?
items.derived: Configure supervisory review and approval workflows for all high-value transactions processed by unattended bots, ensuring no transaction exceeds a defined threshold without human authorization
items.derivationNotes: The bot's service account can initiate/approve/post; supervisory review for high-value transactions is the most critical SOD control.

items.prompt: How many distinct performance obligations exist in Crestline's contract with Regional Hospital?
items.derived: Two — equipment delivery and installation service
items.derivationNotes: Equipment and installation are distinct; the volume rebate is variable consideration, not a separate obligation.

items.prompt: Enter the amount of revenue Crestline should allocate to the equipment performance obligation (round to nearest whole dollar).
items.derivationNotes: DL-069 corrected item. Rebate excluded (Q4 constraint); equipment = 600,000 x 520,000/630,000 = 495,238.

items.prompt: When should Crestline recognize revenue for the equipment portion of the contract?
items.derived: On October 15 when the equipment is delivered to the hospital
items.derivationNotes: Equipment is satisfied at a point in time — control transfers on delivery (October 15).

items.prompt: Under the most likely amount method, what amount of variable consideration should Crestline include in the transaction price for the volume rebate?
items.derived: $0 — the rebate should be excluded until the threshold is met
items.derivationNotes: 60% probability does not meet the probable threshold; the rebate is constrained to $0.

items.prompt: If Crestline subsequently receives a contract modification on November 1 that adds $80,000 of additional equipment (standalone price $75,000) to the original contract, how should the modification be accounted for?
items.derived: As a separate contract because the additional goods are distinct and priced at standalone selling price
items.derivationNotes: The additional equipment is distinct and priced near standalone selling price, so it is a separate contract under ASC 606-10-25-12.

items.prompt: Enter the net realizable value (NRV) per unit for tablets.
Enter the total inventory write-down amount Harbor must record at December 31, 2026.
items.derivationNotes: All product lines have cost < NRV (laptops 680<807.50, tablets 220<228, accessories 35<39.90), so write-down = 0.

items.prompt: What is the appropriate accounting treatment regarding inventory write-downs for Harbor at December 31, 2026?
items.derived: Record no journal entry because cost does not exceed NRV for any product line
items.derivationNotes: No write-down required — cost is below NRV for every product line.

items.prompt: How does the inventory write-down affect Harbor's current ratio and gross margin percentage?
items.derived: Neither ratio is affected because no write-down exists — cost is below NRV for every product line
items.derivationNotes: No write-down means no impact on current assets or COGS.

items.prompt: Exhibit 2 shows the prior year carried $760,000 at cost and $745,000 at LCNRV (a $15,000 write-down) with a 32.5% gross margin. Given this year's $0 write-down from Q2, what trend judgment should Controller David Park report?
items.derived: Write-downs fell from $15,000 to $0, removing a prior-year drag on gross margin — directionally favorable
items.derivationNotes: The write-down drag disappeared (15,000 -> 0), directionally favorable vs the prior-year margin.

items.prompt: Enter the direct material price variance for March. Indicate unfavorable variances as negative numbers.
Enter the direct material quantity variance for March. Indicate unfavorable variances as negative numbers.
Enter the direct labor efficiency variance for March. Indicate unfavorable variances as negative numbers.
Based on the variance results, which of the following interpretations is most appropriate?
items.derived: The unfavorable material price variance may have caused the unfavorable quantity variance if lower-quality materials were purchased
items.derivationNotes: Classic variance interaction: lower-quality (cheaper) materials can cause more waste/usage.

items.prompt: Which variance should Apex investigate first, considering both materiality and controllability?
items.derived: The direct material quantity variance because it is the largest unfavorable variance and is controllable by production
items.derivationNotes: The material quantity variance is the largest unfavorable variance and is within the production manager's control.
